what:
HIGH (code audit CA-A10-001, MEASURED 2026-09-27): docs/claude/system-actions.md §3.5 ('Dispatcher trust contract') names a fixed 8-action 'Tier-2 set' requiring a PM-side-Claude operator ping before dispatch (pull-and-deploy, restart-bot-service, reboot-vm, enable-closed-flat-invariant, disable-closed-flat-invariant, backfill-pnl-nulls, set-account-mode, fix-data-dir), while .github/workflows/system-actions.yml's own Validate step classifies 75 of the 91 allowlisted actions as tier=2. A PM-side Claude session (this session's own dispatcher class) following §3.5's literal text has no textual instruction to ping the operator before autonomously dispatching any of the other 67 tier=2 actions, including several that write trade_journal.db money fields (backfill-broker-order-id, backfill-exit-labels, backfill-broker-truth-costs, backfill-fabricated-exits, mark-operator-flattened, migrate-closed-at-iso) or touch exchange credentials (rotate-account-keys, init-diag-token). Three other counts of 'which actions are Tier 2' exist in the same repo and disagree with each other too: §3's own bullet lists (56 explicit, 22 of 91 actions undeclared entirely), §2's allowlist table (missing 14 of 91 actions' rows, and for 2 -- inspect-insights, kick-insights -- stating Tier 1 where the workflow says tier=2), and tests/ops/test_system_actions_workflow.py's TIER_2_ACTIONS (70, itself never cross-checked against §3.5 or §2 by any guard -- confirmed via `python3 -m pytest tests/ops/test_system_actions_workflow.py -q`, 396 passed, none of which compare these lists to each other). Not clear from the doc's own text whether §3.5's 8-action list was ever intended as the operative ping gate or is simply stale from an earlier, smaller allowlist (INFERRED, not settled) -- this is exactly the ambiguity the operator should resolve. Full finding + evidence: docs/audits/code-audit-2026-09-27/CA-A10.findings.jsonl id CA-A10-001. Proposed fix: reconcile all four sources to one, and add a pytest guard asserting equality (tests/ops/test_system_actions_workflow.py already has the TIER_2_ACTIONS/EXPECTED_ACTIONS machinery to extend).
